arguments.summary: Credential compromise incident initiated via phishing attack on finance user jsmith@corp.local. Adversary deployed Cobalt Strike beacon from malicious Outlook attachment, established C2 communication, and conducted Kerberoasting attacks against high-privilege service accounts (svc_sql_prod, svc_exchange_admin, svc_sccm) using RC4-encrypted TGS requests. Lateral movement observed via SMB to file server. Prompt credential reset prevented escalation to domain compromise.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Config {
    meta:
        description = "Detects embedded Cobalt Strike beacon configuration in memory or file"
        author = "SOC Threat Intel Team"
        severity = "critical"
    strings:
        $a = { 2e 72 63 64 2e 63 73 72 63 } // ".rcd.cs" in XOR or base64 encoded form
        $b = "windows/beacon" wide ascii
        $c = { 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] 68 [4] e8 } // push pattern common in beacon stagers
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: Credential compromise incident initiated via phishing against user CORP\jsmith on endpoint WS-FIN-042. Adversary deployed Cobalt Strike beacon using malicious PowerShell and DLL sideloading from Outlook. Lateral movement attempts detected via SMB and Kerberos exploitation (Kerberoasting) targeting high-privilege service accounts on domain controller DC-PROD-01. IOCs confirm alignment with APT29 tradecraft. Immediate containment actions included password and MFA reset for compromised user. No full domain compromise confirmed.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_Loader {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory-resident Cobalt Strike beacon via runtime DLL loading pattern"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        tlp = "amber"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
    strings:
        $a = { 68 00 30 00 00 68 [4] 00 00 00 E8 [4] 83 C4 08 89 45 FC }
        $b = "Crypt32" fullword ascii
        $c = "kernel32" fullword ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: Suspected Cobalt Strike compromise on endpoint WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) attributed to user CORP\jsmith. Initial access likely via phishing (T1566.001), followed by execution via rundll32.exe loading unsigned DLL (T1218.011). Host established C2 beaconing to 198.51.100.23 over HTTPS (T1071.001), attempted Kerberos TGT brute-force (T1558.003), and performed lateral movement via SMB to file server (T1021.002). Host file modification (T1565.001) observed. No evidence of data exfiltration or ransomware deployment. UEBA scored risk as low due to normal access patterns. EDR and SIEM correlation confirmed malicious activity.

IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beacon signature (ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2)

Lateral movement via SMB to internal file server WS-FIN-050
Anomalous outbound traffic alert triggered based on JA3 fingerprint and entropy analysis
Containment actions initiated: C2 IP blocked at firewall, host isolated
User CORP\jsmith credentials reset, MFA re-enrollment required
Host scanned and remediated; no persistence mechanisms found beyond memory-resident payload

detection:
  selection:

description: Detects rundll32 loading DLLs from the user temp directory, commonly abused by malware.
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate software installers (rare)
author: SOC Team

arguments.summary: Critical compromise involving service account 'svc_deploy_prod' which was used from an unauthorized host (10.0.6.31) to perform privilege escalation and lateral movement within the Active Directory environment. Golden Ticket attack indicators were detected in Kerberos TGT metadata. Immediate actions included revocation of all sessions and API keys for the service account and network isolation of the source host. No malware was detected on the endpoint during full EPP scan, suggesting fileless or memory-resident attack vector.

timeline.description: Initial suspicious activity: Port scan from IP 10.0.6.31 detected and logged by IDS (low severity).
Normal authentication by helpdesk user from host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). No anomalies observed.
Anomalous authentication: svc_deploy_prod logs in from unauthorized host 10.0.6.31 and performs 14 privileged AD operations within 90 seconds.
UEBA system flags critical anomaly: Unusual login time, geolocation deviation, lateral movement, and privilege escalation attempt.
SIEM correlation confirms Golden Ticket indicators in TGT requests and base64-encoded PowerShell command execution history.
Admin response initiated: Service account 'svc_deploy_prod' sessions and API keys revoked.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 10.0.6.31.
Full endpoint scan of 10.0.6.31 completed with EPP; no threats detected.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious Service Account Login from Non-Standard Host
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
  service: security
conditions:
  - event_id: 4624
  - logon_type: 3
  - user: '*svc_*'
  - not src_ip|cidr: '10.0.6.10/32'
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
    User: '*svc_*'
    SourceIP: '10.0.6.31'
  filter:
    SourceIP:
      - '10.0.6.10'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: critical
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/
description: Detects service account authentication from hosts other than approved ones.
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate failover scenarios (requires exclusion tuning)

rule GoldenTicket_Indicators {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory patterns associated with Golden Ticket attacks via mimikatz artifacts"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1558.001"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $s1 = "kerberos::golden" wide ascii
        $s2 = "/service:krbtgt" wide ascii
        $s3 = "aes256_hmac" wide ascii
        $s4 = "/ptt" wide ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

rule GoldenTicket_Indicators {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory patterns associated with Golden Ticket attacks via mimikatz artifacts"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1558.001"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $s1 = "kerberos::golden" wide ascii
        $s2 = "/service:krbtgt" wide ascii
        $s3 = "aes256_hmac" wide ascii
        $s4 = "/ptt" wide ascii
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: Critical incident involving the compromise of the service account 'svc_deploy_prod'. The account was used from an unauthorized host (10.0.6.31) to perform privilege escalation on Active Directory, including modifications to high-privilege groups such as Domain Admins and Enterprise Admins. Golden Ticket authentication indicators were detected, suggesting potential Kerberos TGT forgery. Immediate actions included revocation of all sessions and API keys for the account and blocking of the source IP at the firewall. No malware was detected on the host during a full EPP scan.

timeline.description: Initial network scan from 10.0.6.31 detected via IDS (signature: ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan) targeting subnet 10.0.1.0/24.
Normal authentication by helpdesk user on WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15).
Anomalous service account activity detected: svc_deploy_prod authenticates from 10.0.6.31 (non-registered host) and performs 14 privileged AD operations.
UEBA system flags activity with anomaly score 0.92; behavioral indicators include unusual login time, new geolocation (Bucharest via VPN), lateral movement, and privilege escalation attempts.
SIEM correlation confirms Golden Ticket indicators in TGT metadata and multiple group membership changes to Domain Admins and Enterprise Admins.
IAM/PAM system revokes all sessions and API keys for svc_deploy_prod.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 10.0.6.31.
Full EPP scan of host 10.0.6.31 completed with no threats detected.

  service_name: '*_update'
detection:

  ImagePath: 'C:\\Windows\\Temp\\*'
  condition: ServiceName and ImagePath
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1035/
description: Detects service installation with '_update' in name from Temp directory, commonly used by adversaries for persistence.

title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation by Non-Admin
id: 5a7d8b9e-1f2c-4d5e-8f9a-1b2c3d4e5f6a
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of scheduled tasks pointing to executable in Temp directories by non-admin users.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 4698
        TaskName|contains: 
            - 'Update'
            - 'Maintenance'
            - 'Sync'
        TaskCommand|contains: 
            - '%TEMP%'
            - '%APPDATA%'
            - '\\Temp\\'
        User|notmatch: '.*\\$(Admin|System).*'
    condition: selection
level: high

The endpoint used DNS tunneling via high-entropy TXT queries to the domain ns1.exfil-c2.example.com, resolving to IP 203.0.113.77. Correlation with prior alerts revealed that the same C2 domain was previously used by WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) in a confirmed Cobalt Strike compromise. Although no malicious artifacts were found on WS-FIN-019 during EDR scan, the source user (CORP\auser) was immediately de-escalated. The exfiltration IP and domain have been blocked at the firewall, and all sessions/API keys for the user were revoked. No data loss was confirmed, but lateral movement patterns and prior C2 activity indicate a broader campaign.

id: 8a9d5b2c-1f3e-4a7b-9c2d-6e5f8a9b1c2d
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries with high entropy subdomains for TXT records to domains previously associated with C2 activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: dns_query
    product: network_sensor
detection:
    selection:
        query_type: TXT
        question:
            contains: '.exfil-c2.example.com'
        subdomain_entropy|float > 3.8
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate high-entropy subdomains (rare)
level: high

arguments.summary: A potential data exfiltration incident was detected involving workstation WS-FIN-019 (10.0.4.19) attempting to transfer 2.3 GB of data to external IP 203.0.113.77 via DNS tunneling using the domain ns1.exfil-c2.example.com. The domain is linked to prior Cobalt Strike C2 activity from another compromised host (WS-FIN-042). Despite EDR showing no malicious processes and AV scanning clean, the behavioral pattern and IOCs strongly indicate exfiltration. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall and resetting the user's credentials. No malware was detected on the host during a full scan.

arguments.rule_content:
title: High-Volume DNS TXT Queries with High Entropy Subdomains
description: Detects potential DNS tunneling by identifying high-volume DNS TXT queries with high entropy subdomains, often used in data exfiltration.
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
  service: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryType: 'TXT'
  subdomain_entropy:
    SubdomainEntropy|gt: 3.8
  volume:
    Count|gt: 50
  timeframe: 5m
condition: selection and subdomain_entropy and volume
severity: critical
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of TXT records for high-entropy identifiers (e.g., DKIM)
level: critical
